query: How can support teams reduce ticket resolution time?

per_column.name: request_type
per_column.rationale: The type of request is an intrinsic property of the ticket that affects resolution time and correlates with how it is handled; it is a common cause / covariate but not something a team decides to reduce resolution time. Not intervenable.

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: Category of the issue is an inherent attribute influencing effort and handling. Not settable by the team; acts as a covariate/confounder.

per_column.name: operational_severity
per_column.rationale: Severity is a fixed property of the incident that drives both handling priority and resolution time. Not an intervenable lever.

per_column.name: affected_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope of impact is an intrinsic characteristic of the incident affecting effort. Not settable by the actor.

per_column.name: technical_complexity
per_column.rationale: Complexity is an inherent difficulty measure that increases resolution time; not a lever a team can set.

per_column.name: escalation_signal
per_column.rationale: Presence of external pressure is a property of the ticket influencing prioritization and time. Not an intervenable treatment.

per_column.name: root_cause_domain
per_column.rationale: The root cause is typically discovered during resolution and lies on the causal path between the issue and time-to-resolve rather than being a pre-treatment confounder.

per_column.name: workaround_available
per_column.rationale: Availability of a workaround is a property of the situation that affects urgency and effort; treated as a covariate.

per_column.name: repro_reliability
per_column.rationale: Reproducibility is an intrinsic property affecting diagnosis effort. Not a lever.

per_column.name: actionability
per_column.rationale: The type of remediation action (config change, hotfix/rollback, process change, documentation, engineering fix) is closest to a decision an actor could make, so it is the only candidate intervenable lever. However it is partly determined by the issue, weakening its interventional status.

per_column.name: requires_external_dependency
per_column.rationale: Whether an external dependency is needed is a property of the issue that lengthens resolution; not directly settable.

per_column.name: data_or_info_provided
per_column.rationale: Whether repro steps/logs are provided reflects an intake process the team could change (e.g., require info), so it is a plausible intervenable lever, though here it is recorded as a passive attribute.

judge.rationale: The query is genuinely interventional ('How can support teams reduce...'), demanding a settable lever plus adjustment for confounders. The schema is dominated by intrinsic properties of the ticket/issue (severity, scope, complexity, reproducibility, request type, dependencies). These function as covariates/confounders and none are named in the query, which is good for adjustment coverage. However, most added columns describe the difficulty of the case rather than a decision the team controls, so genuine intervenable treatments are weak: only 'actionability' and 'data_or_info_provided' come close to settable levers, and even these are largely case-determined attributes rather than clearly assignable interventions. There is no clean process/policy lever (e.g., staffing, tooling, SLA routing, agent action). 'root_cause_domain' is a mediator discovered during resolution and should not be adjusted for. Overall the set supports an attributional/predictive read of resolution time well but only marginally satisfies the strict what-if requirement of an intervenable treatment.
